chunks: And from him, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no Sa'ee required of the rider, but he should hasten a little.

key_terms.الرَّاكِبِ: the rider (one mounted on an animal or vehicle)
key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Sa'ee (the ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person riding during Sa'ee in Hajj?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the flexibility of Sa'ee for those with valid excuses, such as illness or old age, who may ride between Safa and Marwah. The Imam specifies that while the full walking circuit is not obligatory for the rider, they must still 'hasten' or move briskly, preserving the ritual's essence of active devotion rather than passive observation. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj) while maintaining the core spirit of the act.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘There is no Sa’ee to be performed by the rider, but it is in order to expedite something’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One riding is not required to perform Sa‘y (walking faster like running slowly) but they should hasten to a certain degree.’”
